case.pattern_description: Threshold structuring on a compromised card: 4 online purchases ($463.88, $466.93, $459.07, $470.55) placed within about an hour, each kept just under $500, the level at which authorisation checks tighten. It affects cardholders whose card numbers are already compromised and matches five closed cases the bank confirmed but could not map to a known typology; the agent found it by scanning the card's window for clusters of same-band amounts.

sar.narrative: Customer C00466, holder of card C00466-K1, is the subject of this report. Between 2016-11-21 20:00 and 2016-11-21 20:24, 4 transaction(s) totalling $1,860.43 were made on the card online from device profile 'Windows |  | chrome 64.0 | ': $463.88 (3476601, 2016-11-21 20:00), $466.93 (3476621, 2016-11-21 20:07), $459.07 (3476655, 2016-11-21 20:22), $470.55 (3476664, 2016-11-21 20:24). Every amount sat just below $500 and the purchases were placed minutes apart, a pattern consistent with deliberately staying under an authorisation threshold. The activity is suspicious because: 4 online purchases within 24 minutes, each between $400 and $500 ($463.88, $466.93, $459.07, $470.55; total $1,860.43). It closely resembles earlier confirmed fraud cases CC-3748, CC-4124, CC-3841. The bank has recommended blocking and reissuing the card, placed linked cards under monitoring where applicable, and retains the transaction, device and investigation records as supporting documentation.
